Approving plans, merging and deploying stay with a person.

app.faq.alone.a: No. The AI always works together with people and other agents: it takes cards and opens PRs, but approving plans, merging and approving deploys stay with a person who holds the required role.
app.faq.alone.q: Can the AI run the project on its own?
app.faq.approve.a:
Click the card to open its details. When a plan is waiting, "Approve plan", "Reject plan" and "Adjust" (describe the change) show up. It needs the write role, by default.
You can also answer on the GitHub issue itself with Aprovado (approve), Rejeitado (reject) or the change. The agent resumes where it stopped, without planning again.
app.faq.approve.q: How do I approve, reject or adjust the plan?
app.faq.audit.a: Every action taken through the panel or a token: starting a card, answering a plan, merging, updating a branch, approving workflows, approving or rejecting a deploy, changing budget, connections and roles, including denied attempts. The card details show that card's audit.
app.faq.audit.q: What goes into the audit log?
app.faq.blocked.a: Open the card and read the agent's last comment and the failed run. Fix what was missing (description, permission, budget) and start the card again, or ask for a change to the plan.
app.faq.blocked.q: A card went to "Blocked". Now what?
app.faq.budget.a:
In Settings → Project budget (admin, by default). There are per-card limits (cost in US$, minutes and steps) and an optional monthly ceiling, which starts with no ceiling.
At 80% of any limit the agent is warned; at 100% it stops and the card waits for a person. Once the monthly ceiling is reached, no new card starts.
app.faq.budget.q: Where do I set the budget?
app.faq.chat.a:
The orchestrator chat runs only with an AI provider set up with an API key (Anthropic, OpenAI or Gemini) in Connections. Without a key it is off and the panel says why. The Claude Code subscription token runs the executor only, never the chat.
This does not stop the work: cards, agents and your AI connected through MCP keep working.
app.faq.chat.q: Why is the chat with the orchestrator off?
app.faq.claim.a:
Through the MCP claim_card tool. It labels the card agent:claimed and leaves on the issue who took it, which agent and which specialties. Other collaborators see it on the board and pick another card.
When it gives up or ends without a PR, the AI uses release_card to put the card back in Backlog. To say something, it uses comment_card.
app.faq.claim.q: How does my AI take a card without stepping on anyone?
app.faq.columns.a:
- Backlog: open issues not started yet. "Queued for the agent" means the card was sent to the agent and waits for a run.
- Agent working: an agent run is going on right now for the card.
- Waiting for a human: the agent posted a plan or a question and waits for a person.
- Blocked: the run failed or the agent stopped with nothing to approve; open the card.
- In review (PR): the agent opened a pull request waiting for review and merge.
- Done: closed cards (the most recent; the rest are on GitHub).
app.faq.columns.q: What does each board column mean?
app.faq.connectai.q: How do I connect my AI (Claude Code, Antigravity, Kiro, Gemini CLI, Codex…)?
app.faq.connections.a:
There an admin picks the provider and model of each flow role and keeps each provider's secrets (an API key or the Claude Code subscription token). Secrets never go into the repository.
Today only the orchestrator chat actually uses that choice; for the other roles it is only read.
app.faq.connections.q: What is the Connections screen for?
app.faq.cost.a: It is an estimate in dollars and tokens of what planning and execution used, priced at the equivalent API rate. It is not an invoice: with a subscription, the real charge follows your plan with the provider.
app.faq.cost.q: What is the cost shown on a card?
app.faq.create.a:
Use "New card" at the top of the Backlog column, with a title and a description of what needs to be done. Creating an issue straight on GitHub works too: it shows up in Backlog.
A good description says the goal, what is out of scope and how to tell it is done.
app.faq.create.q: How do I create a card?
app.faq.deploy.a:
Production deploys waiting for approval show up in "Pending deploys". Approve or reject them (maintain role, by default). An old stuck deploy blocks the queue: the panel warns you, and cancelling the replaced one frees the queue.
A change reaches app.tradvia.org only after the merge into main and the deploy approval.
app.faq.deploy.q: How do I approve a deploy?
app.faq.empty.a:
- Use app.tradvia.org and sign in with GitHub. At another address the panel reads GitHub without signing in and hits the limit of 60 requests per hour.
- Sign out and back in: an old session can leave the screen without data.
- Make sure the address has no filters (from, to, executor, fcard, status), which narrow the cards.
- Read the message in the bar above the board. With no message, open the browser console (F12) and note the first red error.
- Reload without cache: Ctrl+Shift+R (Cmd+Shift+R on Mac).
app.faq.empty.q: The panel is empty or has no cards. What do I check?
app.faq.invite.a:
Access follows GitHub. In the repository, go to Settings → Collaborators → Add people, pick the person and the role (Write is the usual one to work on cards).
The person accepts the invitation (by e-mail and at github.com/notifications) and signs in to Tradvia with their own account. For their pull request to be accepted, they also sign the CLA when the bot asks on their first PR.
app.faq.invite.q: How do I add a person to the project?
app.faq.isolation.a: No. Each project is its repository: cards, costs, budget, roles, tokens and audit are kept apart. A token created in one project does not work in another.
app.faq.isolation.q: Can one project's data show up in another?
app.faq.manager.a:
It is an AI below the project's owner, with a manager-type token. By default it only follows and organizes: it reads the board, comments and suggests.
An admin can grant it, for up to 90 days, reordering the backlog and approving plans, and take that back at any time. It never merges, deploys, or touches budget, connections or roles.
app.faq.merge.a:
Open the card in "In review (PR)". The details show the summary, the changed files and the checks. When all is green, use "Merge (squash)" (maintain role, by default). If the branch is behind main, use "Update branch" first.
This depends on the GitHub App permissions on the repository; if the button does not work, merge on GitHub.
app.faq.merge.q: How do I review and merge a PR?
app.faq.missing.a: The published version may be older: the panel is updated only after the merge into main and the production deploy approval. The Documentation page shows the real status of each capability.
app.faq.missing.q: A feature described here is missing from the panel.
app.faq.nobutton.a: Buttons only show up for whoever holds the required role in that project. Check your role at the top of the page and in Settings. If you were just given access on GitHub, sign out and back in.
app.faq.nobutton.q: The button I expected (Start, Merge, Approve…) is missing.
app.faq.nothingrunning.a: That column only shows cards with an agent run going on at that moment. If no card was started, or all of them finished, it stays empty. Start a card from Backlog for the agent to begin.
app.faq.nothingrunning.q: Why is no card in "Agent working"?
app.faq.pending.a: The bell counts what is waiting for you right now: plans to answer, PRs to review, deploys to approve, stuck queues. Click it to see the list and open each item.
app.faq.policy.a: In Settings → Project roles and risk, admin only. It holds the minimum role of each action (start a card, approve a plan, merge, deploy…) and who must approve each risk level of the agent's actions. It takes effect at once for people, agents and tokens of this project.
app.faq.policy.q: Where do I change who can do what?
app.faq.project.a: A project shows up when you have access to its repository on GitHub and the Tradvia GitHub App is installed on it. If you were just invited, accept the invitation on GitHub, then sign out of Tradvia and back in.
app.faq.project.q: Why don't I see my project?
app.faq.revoke.a: In "Connect my AI", in the "My tokens in this project" list, click "Revoke". The token stops working at once. If you think a token leaked, revoke it and create a new one.
app.faq.revoke.q: How do I revoke a token?
app.faq.roles.a:
The role comes from GitHub (read < triage < write < maintain < admin). The defaults are:
- read: sees the project's panel.
- triage: also starts cards.
- write: also approves, rejects or adjusts plans and mentions the assistant.
- maintain: also merges PRs, updates the PR branch, approves deploys and takes over the live session.
- admin: also changes the budget, connections, and the project's roles and risk.
An admin can change these minimums in Settings, per project. Managing connections always stays with admin.
app.faq.signin.a:
Click "Sign in with GitHub" at the top of the page and authorize. Tradvia has no password of its own: your identity is your GitHub account.
Once signed in, the top shows your login and your role in the open project.
app.faq.startcard.a:
On the Backlog card, click "Start" (triage role or above, by default). Tradvia labels the issue agent:ready and the agent begins with the plan.
Each run uses the project's AI provider quota and counts against the budget. When the monthly ceiling is reached, no new card starts.
app.faq.startcard.q: How do I send a card to the agent?
app.faq.what.a:
Tradvia is the panel where people and AI agents work together on the cards of a GitHub repository. Each card is an issue: the agent plans, a person approves, the agent carries it out and opens a pull request, and a person reviews and merges it.
Everything is bound to the repository: cards, costs, budget, roles, tokens and audit of one project never show up in another.
app.faq.who.a: When a person or their AI takes a card, the card shows "With @login", the agent used and its declared specialties. Click the card to see its timeline and audit.
app.faq.who.q: How do I know who is working on a card?
app.faq.workflows.a: GitHub holds the workflows of first-time contributors. In the PR details, a maintainer clicks "Approve workflows" after looking at the code, and the checks run.
app.faq.workflows.q: A PR from an outside collaborator does not run its checks. What do I do?
app.faq.yml.a: Because these settings now live on Tradvia, per project, not in a file. The budget, interactions and risk sections of .tradvia.yml are ignored, and the Settings screen tells you when they are still there.
app.faq.yml.q: Why does changing .tradvia.yml not change the budget or the roles?

docs.cap.connections.body: The "Connections" screen (admin role): provider and model per flow role (planner/executor/reviewer/orchestrator), and each AI provider's secret (an API key, or the Claude Code subscription token). Today only the orchestrator role (the chat) actually uses the choice; the other roles still only read the configuration, without applying it. The chat works only with an AI provider configured with an API key (Anthropic, OpenAI or Gemini); without one it is off and the panel says why. The Claude Code subscription token runs the executor only, never the chat. An API key is the only method for Anthropic/Gemini/OpenAI — none of the three currently offers a browser login for third-party apps the way the Claude Code subscription does (see ADR 0019).

docs.trouble.1.body: Use the panel published at app.tradvia.org. In a local copy or at another address, the panel reads GitHub without signing in, and GitHub allows only 60 requests per hour for your IP. If “GitHub API rate limit reached” appears, wait up to an hour or open app.tradvia.org.
